picks.name: VanEck Gold Miners
risks: volatile stock in a risk-off market

drivers.title: AI and tech stocks crash after Democratic sweep on fears of tighter AI rules; Trump blames voters
drivers.rationale: The VIX spiked 70% to 28 and gold rose 1% -> de-risking favours gold miners, utilities and staples over small caps and discretionary in the near term.

drivers.title: Tankers hit mines and a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz; ceasefire odds fall
drivers.rationale: Attacks on shipping plus falling ceasefire odds and talk of a post-midterm campaign -> energy majors gain, airlines lose. Brent is already +12% in 20 days, so the size is moderate. This cuts against yesterday's low-confidence call that diplomacy would ease the oil premium; the money has moved toward escalation.

drivers.title: US warns allies of possible Iran strikes after midterms; Hormuz incidents continue
drivers.rationale: A signalled post-midterm campaign plus US escorts through Hormuz -> risk of renewed fighting -> energy majors up, airlines down. The warning partly repeats yesterday's report, and ceasefire odds rose rather than fell, so confidence is moderate.

drivers.title: EU invites states to use €21.3bn of SAFE defence loans; Russian strike on Dnipro station
drivers.rationale: SAFE money being called up -> concrete procurement funding for European primes. WDEF.MI is flat this week, so this is not priced. US pressure to tone down Russia rhetoric is a mild offset.

drivers.title: UK pledges defence spending of 3% of GDP by 2030; Netherlands adds Ukraine aid while Italy delays
drivers.rationale: A firmer UK path to 3% of GDP -> more domestic procurement -> BAE Systems is the main UK beneficiary.

drivers.title: Spain and Italy add Ukraine military aid; EU disburses €4.36bn; NATO speeds counter-drone procurement
drivers.rationale: Steady European aid packages and fast-tracked NATO counter-drone buying -> order flow for air-defence and electronics names like Thales, Leonardo and Rheinmetall. WDEF is +6.8% in 20 days, so the size is small.

drivers.title: Qatari LNG carrier struck in the Gulf as Hormuz tanker attacks continue
drivers.rationale: First attack on a Qatari LNG carrier -> threat to the main remaining Gulf LNG flows into a tight winter -> TTF higher (+5.4% Friday) -> European chemicals lose, US gas producers gain. TTF is already +39% in 20 days, so the size is held moderate.

drivers.title: QatarEnergy buys US LNG, including a 20-year Woodside deal, to hedge Hormuz risk
drivers.rationale: Even Qatar now contracts US LNG long-term -> more Gulf Coast liquefaction demand -> more US feedgas -> support for the largest US gas producer. Henry Hub rose 4.8% yesterday.

drivers.title: Qatar extends LNG force majeure to Italy's Edison until year-end
drivers.rationale: Less Qatari LNG into Italy through winter -> TTF stays high -> margin pressure on European chemicals, support for US gas producers. TTF already +38% in 20 days, so mostly priced.

drivers.title: Iran calls US reply to Hormuz plan 'unconvincing' as tankers burn and Trump confirms strikes
drivers.rationale: Mines and guerrilla attacks keep hitting tankers while talks stall -> war-risk premiums and freight rates stay elevated. BOAT is -1.8% in 5 days on deal hopes, which leaves room to rebound; Trump's no-strike stance limits the upside.

drivers.title: US carries out 'defensive' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near Hormuz
drivers.rationale: Strikes on Iranian positions beside the strait and continued attacks on tankers -> war-risk premiums stay high in the short run even as talks progress. BOAT fell 3.3% on Monday, so it has room to rebound if the strikes escalate; both sides call the action limited, so confidence is low.
